title: feat(mig): implement verified MS7-MIG-V02 candidate
body:
MS7-MIG-V02 — Implementation Candidate

Issue: Refs #35
PR: #53
Status: DRAFT — NOT READY FOR MERGE

Scope

Implements MS7-MIG-V02 on the accepted V01/I01 integration baseline.

  • Content delivery and immutable published-release projections.

  • Grades GET API with Django-compatible signed keyset cursors.

  • Staff read APIs with authorization and permission checks.

  • Redirects, SEO, static/media compatibility and safe routing.

  • Required HOME alias validation.

  • Pinned-release renderer context for I02 integration.

  • Acceptance evidence, independent audits and regression coverage.

Current Published Candidate

Implementation SHA: 8256cbf4b38e97fc1169fea85f2d558950543be8

Parent SHA: 76d8eac6387a5fde5432a0e8130a881cb6d7ba82

Git tree OID: 74c3014516ec3a2110d2cfec13c8e7afb8ae5024

Branch: ms7-mig-v02-content

Base branch: ms7-mig-react-fastapi

The approved I02 consumer handoff follow-up has been implemented and published as a separate commit on top of the previously verified candidate.

Exact follow-up diff:

Compare 76d8eac...8256cbf

The commit contains:

  • 5 modified files within Ruslan's approved production/test/docs scope.

  • 63 new V02-owned test, verification and trace evidence files.

  • No changes to frozen R02 contracts, historical acceptance evidence, V01/Alembic, frontend, root CI or R03 publication controls.

Follow-up Implementation — I02 Consumer Handoff

Ruslan approved both backend improvements for this existing Draft PR. The internal renderer context shape was agreed with Ilya.

1. Required HOME Alias Validation — Implemented

When a HOME page exists in an immutable published release, ReleaseStore requires the corresponding mandatory alias:

  • URL: /<home-slug>/

  • page_id: ID of the same HOME page.

  • HTTP status: 200.

  • canonical_path: /

For a valid release:

  • / resolves with HTTP 200 and canonical /.

  • /<home-slug>/ resolves with HTTP 200 and canonical /.

Missing or invalid mandatory alias data causes the release to fail closed using the existing safe 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE behavior.

The validation includes negative regression coverage with correctly recalculated manifest/index digests, demonstrating that rejection is caused by the HOME invariant rather than a checksum mismatch.

Additional verified scenarios include:

  • Correct HOME alias.

  • Missing or invalid mandatory alias.

  • Different valid HOME slug.

  • Release without HOME.

  • Correct canonical behavior.

  • No fallback to redirects or a previous valid release when the current active release is invalid.

Alias policy: No expansion of additional HOME aliases is authorized in the current V02 profile. Redirects remain a separate mechanism.

Frozen R02 contracts and public DTOs remain unchanged.

2. Pinned-Release Renderer Context — Implemented

The existing internal callback signature is preserved:

render_page(page, context, canonical_url)

Two internal context fields are provided.

catalogue_full — for /karta-sajta/ only

Contains the complete public catalogue from the same immutable release:

  • grades

  • subjects

  • sections

  • topics

Existing IDs, titles, slugs, ordering and relationships are preserved.

The full catalogue is available independently of the current search query and does not replace filtered search results.

pinned_release — for all public HTML pages

Contains:

  • release_id

  • manifest_digest

These values identify the immutable release selected for the current request.

Compatibility and consistency guarantees:

  • All seven existing catalogue_* context fields retain their semantics.

  • Existing filtering, ordering, canonical URLs and public SEO behavior are preserved.

  • Page data, filtered results, complete catalogue and release identity originate from the same pinned Release.

  • No rereading of the active release descriptor or current database catalogue during rendering.

  • No mixing of R1/R2 data when the active release changes during an in-flight request.

  • Renderer receives isolated copies of page and context data.

  • Nested renderer mutations cannot modify validated Release.pages or Release.index.

  • Existing public Content DTOs and API endpoints remain unchanged.

  • No mandatory Node.js runtime has been introduced.

3. Renderer Mutation Safety — Independently Verified

An independent audit identified a blocking P2 issue: the renderer could previously mutate validated page data through a shared object reference.

The follow-up now passes a deep copy of the page to the renderer.

Regression coverage verifies:

  • Top-level and nested page mutations.

  • Simultaneous page/context mutation.

  • Preservation of validated release data.

  • Correct behavior on subsequent HTTP requests.

  • Consistent pinned-release identity.

  • Safe 503 behavior when the renderer raises an exception.

Independent re-audit result: P2 CLOSED.

4. Evidence Encoding — Independently Resolved

A previous P3 finding concerned SHA256 mismatches in two source_utf8 evidence helpers.

The final independent re-audit established that the finding resulted from decoding UTF-8 JSON using CP1251. The original bytes and recorded SHA256 values were correct.

Additional explicit UTF-8, raw-byte and physical-read verification was introduced without modifying historical evidence.

Independent re-audit classification: P3 ORIGINAL FINDING INVALID.

Independent Verification — Current Follow-up

The implementation was independently reviewed before publication.

Final technical verdict: READY FOR FOLLOW-UP PUBLICATION

Blocking findings: 0

Verified Regression Results

Verification | Result -- | -- V02 | 118 PASS, including 50 PostgreSQL tests V01 | 34 PASS R02 | 63 PASS R02A | 30 PASS R03A | 41 PASS Repository verification | 8/8 PASS Django | 109 PASS R03 | 18 PASS Harness | 73 PASS Content parity | 279 pages / 263 topics PASS

The independent review confirmed:

  • Required HOME alias validation.

  • Safe failure for invalid immutable releases.

  • Correct full catalogue and pinned-release context.

  • Page and context mutation isolation.

  • Preservation of Content, Grades, staff and HTTP regressions.

  • Frozen contracts and ownership boundaries.

  • Integrity of the follow-up evidence.

The follow-up source was independently audited before committing. The published Git commit identity has been verified locally and against the remote branch.

Important: independent R03/Task CI verification of the new published SHA and renewed human Task Approval remain separate acceptance gates.

Previous Published Candidate — Historical Verified Baseline

The original V02 candidate was:

Implementation SHA: 76d8eac6387a5fde5432a0e8130a881cb6d7ba82

Parent SHA: 0c03197e23f69a233c0fcf8bdffa336feca20b92

Git tree OID: dbad1e853dff354c5d3255755afb5cc32e0ad279

Completed Verification for the Previous SHA

  • V02: 86 PASS, including 40 PostgreSQL tests.

  • V01: 34 PASS.

  • R02 / R02A / R03A: 63 / 30 / 41 PASS.

  • Independent F01/F02 audit: CLOSED.

  • Publication verifier v3: independently technically verified.

  • External R03 publication gate: VERIFIED.

  • Published candidate gate and Task CI: VERIFIED by Ruslan.

  • No technical blockers were identified by Ruslan for that candidate.

Historical verification receipts:

  • GitHub Actions run 38637910883

  • GitHub Actions run 38642117604

The approved publication policy preserves 40 exact whitespace exceptions and 73 separate raw-preservation paths.

For the historical evidence snapshot, full Git whitespace checks were documented as FAIL / exit 2, while the approved scoped checks were PASS / exit 0.

The follow-up commit's staged changes passed the ordinary and cr-at-eol whitespace checks before publication.

The historical successful CI runs and approvals apply to SHA 76d8eac6387a5fde5432a0e8130a881cb6d7ba82 only. They do not constitute approval of the current HEAD.

V02 / I02 Ownership and Integration Boundaries

V02 / Vladimir:

  • Immutable release validation.

  • Mandatory HOME alias.

  • Backend catalogue and renderer context.

  • Pinned-release consistency.

  • Isolation of validated data from renderer mutation.

  • Backend regression coverage.

I02 / Ilya:

  • HTML renderer.

  • Grouping and labels.

  • No-JS catalogue presentation.

  • Escaping and XSS safety.

  • SEO/SSG and browser behavior.

  • Consumer integration tests.

Renderer wiring: requires coordination with Ruslan and Ilya, preserving ADR-0006 and avoiding an obligatory Node.js runtime.

Additional integration considerations:

  • Lossless Python/TypeScript int64 ID handling.

  • Retention of the pinned release during in-flight requests when activation changes R1 → R2.

  • Actual HTML/no-JS/SSG/browser validation on the new implementation SHA.

  • Production V04 activation/recovery lifecycle remains outside the verified V02 scope.

Change Scope and Preservation

The approved follow-up modified exactly these five tracked files:

  1. backend/content/releases.py

  2. backend/infrastructure/http/app.py

  3. backend/tests/v02/test_unit.py

  4. backend/tests/v02/test_http.py

  5. backend/infrastructure/http/README.md

The new evidence is stored within the V02-owned acceptance area:

  • docs/acceptance/MS7-MIG-V02/i02-handoff-followup-20261015/

  • docs/acceptance/MS7-MIG-V02/i02-handoff-p2-p3-20261015/

Frozen R02/R02A/R03A contracts, V01/Alembic, historical approval records, frontend, root CI, R03 controls and V04 ownership remain unchanged.

Pending Acceptance Gates — Current SHA

The following checks and decisions remain pending for:

8256cbf4b38e97fc1169fea85f2d558950543be8

  1. Independent R03 publication verification of the exact published follow-up SHA.

  2. Applicable current Task CI and verification receipts for that SHA.

  3. Ilya's I02 consumer compatibility review and integration test confirmation.

  4. Coordination of renderer wiring and remaining Python/TypeScript boundary questions.

  5. Ruslan's renewed final V02 Task Approval.

  6. Separate explicit authorization to merge.

Previous approvals and successful runs must not be treated as approval for the modified candidate.

PR STATUS: DRAFT — NOT READY FOR MERGE.

Issue #35 remains open.
